newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land interested in more Parkway shares - CEO.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land interested in more Parkway shares - CEO.

text.p: DBS Land Ltd, which just announced plans to buy a 19.16 percent stake in Parkway Holdings, is interested in more Parkway shares, a top DBS official said on Wednesday.
Han Cheng Fong, deputy chairman and group chief executive officer, was speaking to analysts and reporters after the launch of DBS Land's initial public offer of subsidiary Australand.
Asked if DBS Land was interested in more Parkway shares, he said: "We just took a sizeable chunk of Parkway which cost us about Singapore $391 million...we are not in a big hurry."
"What I would say is that if there are more shares available at the correct price, of course we would be interested."
Han said it was too early for speculation about whether DBS Land was interested in making a general offer for Parkway shares.
Under Singapore takeover rules, a general offer would be triggered if a party accumulated a 25 percent stake in a listed company.
"It is a bit too early to talk about taking over the company, we only have about 19 percent."
"The first thing that we wish to do is to approach the other shareholders to see how see how we can work together with them," Han said.

Currently, Parkway is controlled and managed by Malaysia's Tan family which holds about 24 percent of the company. Together with their long time partners, the Ang and Ho families, the group holds some 44 percent of Parkway.
DBS Land had been in contact with the Tan family prior to Tuesday's public announcement that it had agreed to buy the 19.16 percent Parkway stake from Malaysia's Hospital Pantai.
"The moment we signed the agreement, I had a chat with (Parkway managing director) Tony Tan and we had a few exchanges, friendly ones," Han said.

He also said the company would make a decision within the next six months as to whether it would increase its Parkway stake to at least 20 percent, which would allow it to equity account Parkway's profits.
Han dismissed analysts' comments that DBS Land paid an expensive price for Parkway.
"We don't think it is expensive. If we thought it was expensive, we won't have bought it," he said.
He said Parkway was "a good company" and there would be synergies between the two companies in the business of healthcare and property.

DBS Land has identified healthcare as a new core business for the group. Parkway is a major healthcare provider in the region, owning several hospitals including the prestigious Mount Elizabeth and Gleneagles Hospitals in Singapore.
